## Contact Information
For questions regarding this report, please contact Matthew Saponaro, Ph.D., Director of the [Technology Service Center](https://www.sites.udel.edu/technology-service-center) at University of Delaware

## Motivation

The purpose of this inventory is to identify, measure, and document large, mature trees in Rittenhouse Park and along parts of Redd Park Trail, Redd Trail 1, and Redd Trail 3 in William M. Redd Jr. Park. The collected data will support planning, maintenance, ecological assessments, and long-term urban forestry initiatives.

## Overview

Across Rittenhouse Park and Redd Park trail sections, 117 trees were inventoried. Of the trees recorded, 105 (89.74%) are large, mature trees, and 12 (10.26%) are slightly smaller than large, mature trees. In this project, only large, mature trees were intentionally sought to be measured; however, some measured trees were smaller than the criteria for a large, mature tree and were recorded regardless. The criteria for "large, mature trees" were defined as follows:

Large Mature Trees: Any trees with a Diameter at Breast Height (DBH) >= 20 inches

## Inventoried Locations

The tree inventory was completed across sections of Rittenhouse Park and Redd Park Trail to collect information on tree locations, characteristics, and overall conditions. The survey focused on trees located within a 15-foot buffer of the trail area to create a consistent study boundary and capture trees that may impact or interact with the surrounding trail environment.

Figure 1 displays the inventoried locations and provides a visual overview of the areas included in the study. The selected locations represent a mix of trail and park settings, allowing for a better understanding of tree distribution and patterns throughout the area.
